solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swell dance skirt

parts.note: to swell up is to puff, as cheeks do
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A smart dance skirt is admired as a swell outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffball is a full, bunched-up style of skirt gathered at the hem.

clue.text: Standing pier gets demolished

indicators.note: a demolished structure is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside pier is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in the sense of status or reputation is a synonym of prestige.

clue.text: Dowdy woman's fine bottom

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
the rump is the buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone compliments a plain woman on her nice behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a drab, unfashionably dressed woman.

clue.text: Armed thief in prison also

parts.note: a brig is a prison, originally on a ship
and means as well, also

explanation.surface: A robber with a weapon is in jail too.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, especially one of a gang robbing travellers.

clue.text: Den left warm and dry

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it fully

explanation.surface: A room is left warm and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: To air clothes in British usage is to put them somewhere warm to finish drying.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den.

clue.text: Two articles about spymaster with girl

indicators.note: the two article letters go round the other pieces, one on each side

parts.note: two copies of the indefinite article a
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
and means together with

explanation.surface: A spy chief turns up with a young woman and a couple of grammar terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The two A's sit either side of M plus AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, used here as an example of the general word.

clue.text: Swallow last of Chianti, an Italian drink

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family

indicators.note: the final letter of the wine's name is taken

explanation.surface: Someone downs the dregs of a Chianti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Martini is a brand of Italian vermouth, a drink made in Turin.

clue.text: Sat in gaol, distraught, longing for the past

indicators.note: distraught means very upset, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A prisoner sat in a cell, upset and yearning for old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental yearning for a former time.

clue.text: Patriotic song from worker on border

parts.note: a worker is a kind of ant
a hem is the edged border of cloth

explanation.surface: A labourer sings a national song from the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A national anthem is a song of patriotic praise for a country.

clue.text: Learning game in publication

indicators.note: the game's letters are placed inside the publication word

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a book or paper
RU stands for rugby union, a ball game

explanation.surface: Someone studies a game written up in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarly knowledge gained through study, i.e. learning as a noun.

clue.text: Old Harry, perhaps?

parts.note: Old Harry is a jocular name for the Devil, like Old Nick; Harry is also the pet form of Henry

explanation.definitionFit: An informal or familiar substitute name such as Old Harry is a moniker of this kind.

clue.text: I must enter remainder to take exam again

indicators.note: the letter I has to go inside the word for remainder

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: A student is told they must go back in with the rest to sit the test again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is a British term for sitting an exam a second time after failing.

clue.text: Spinner, bowler, maybe seen in film

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a bowler is one example of a hat

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a spin bowler is spotted in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinner and bowler suggest cricket, but they are a toy and a hat. Top Hat is the 1935 Astaire and Rogers musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is a classic Hollywood musical picture starring Fred Astaire.

clue.text: Start to play the part of Evita abroad

parts.note: to act is to perform a role

indicators.note: abroad means scattered or astray, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor begins to play the musical heroine on a foreign tour.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT is followed by IVATE, the rearranged letters of EVITA.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a machine is to set it going, i.e. start it.

clue.text: Flag's pattern

definitions.meaning: a model or norm to follow

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means both a banner carried as an emblem and a benchmark or norm.

clue.text: Showing off magnificent still

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
standing means stationary, not moving

explanation.surface: A show-off stands stock still looking magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandstanding means behaving ostentatiously to impress onlookers, as at a stadium stand.

clue.text: Mother in reform school

parts.note: Latin for nourishing mother, used of the school or college one attended, which is what reform school might be for some

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally bounteous mother, denotes one's former school or university.

clue.text: One may get a story about drink with the Queen

parts.note: re means concerning
port is a fortified wine
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone gets a scoop by drinking port with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist's job is to gather news stories.

clue.text: Get nothing wrong? Don't be deceived into thinking otherwise

definitions.meaning: literally, to avoid any error at all

definitions.text: Don't be deceived into thinking otherwise
definitions.meaning: an emphatic phrase meaning be in no doubt, rest assured

explanation.surface: Advice to get everything right, and to be in no doubt about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used both literally for avoiding errors and idiomatically to mean be quite certain.

clue.text: Start to stop out

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop it
off means away or out, as when a light is off

explanation.surface: Someone is told to begin to stop going out.
explanation.definitionFit: The kick-off is the start of a football match, hence any beginning.

clue.text: Small child by bank in squalid quarter

parts.note: a kid is a child
a bank is a row or tier, as of keys or oars

explanation.surface: A small child is found by a river bank in a slum.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is a run-down district where vagrants and down-and-outs live.

clue.text: A meaning that's lost

parts.note: the drift of a remark is its gist or meaning

explanation.surface: A meaning goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means aimless or astray, i.e. lost.

clue.text: Protest about informer being party member

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A political activist joins a protest against a police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the Democratic Party in the US, so is a member of a political party.

clue.text: Complete failure hidden by Mafia's cover-up

indicators.note: the letters needed run unbroken through the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gangland cover-up ends in total disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is an ignominious and total flop, a humiliating collapse.

clue.text: Wonder most of the soldiers returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse order
the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: It is a marvel that most of the troops came back.
explanation.walkthrough: TH (most of THE) and GIS run together then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is a spectacle or marvel, as in the sights of a city.

clue.text: Detailed message, precious

indicators.note: detailed here means de-tailed, its last letter cut off

parts.note: a tweet is a short online message

explanation.surface: A long, detailed message proves precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious in the sense of affectedly dainty or quaint is a near-synonym of twee.

clue.text: Opening bars of 8? Take it away

indicators.note: take, with away, means remove the following word from the hymn

parts.note: the answer to 8 is a hymn; an introit is an anthem sung at the start of a church service
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conductor counts in the start of a hymn and tells the band to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the clue at 8 down, a hymn or anthem; the church anthem INTROIT loses IT. 'Take it away' is also what you say to start a band playing.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the short introductory passage at the start of a piece of music.

clue.text: Total made by county fair

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: A complete total is reckoned up at a county show.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; a county fair is a rural show, which is the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adjective means utter or absolute, as in a downright lie, i.e. total.

clue.text: List of charges resulting from squabble when crossing a river

indicators.note: the squabble word straddles the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
R is the standard map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Ferrymen argue about the fares when crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties, a list of charges.

clue.text: This, in wet areas, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something is suggested to be present wherever things are wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the answer itself, which might well be found in wet areas.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-referring word stands for the answer: salt water from the ocean, found in wet areas.
